title: To-do web app with a saved store
prompt:
Build a to-do web app with index.html, style.css, store.js and app.js (plain JavaScript, no libraries, no build step).
store.js holds the data logic and must also work in Node: end it with `if (typeof module !== "undefined") module.exports = { createStore };`.
createStore(storage) takes an object with getItem(key) and setItem(key, value) (localStorage in the page, a fake in tests) and returns a store with:
- add(text) -> the new item {id, text, done: false}; text is trimmed; empty text throws an Error. Ids are 1, 2, 3... and never reused.
- toggle(id), edit(id, text) (trimmed; empty throws), remove(id); an unknown id throws an Error.
- list(filter) with filter "all" (default), "active" or "done", in the order added.
- clearDone() removes the done items and returns how many it removed.
- counts() -> {all, active, done}.
Every change saves {"nextId": n, "items": [...]} as JSON under the key "todos", and createStore loads what is already saved there (a missing or broken value starts empty).
app.js connects the page: an input and Add button, the list with a checkbox, edit and delete for each item, All/Active/Done filters, the counts, and Clear done. Write a Node test file for store.js too (node test_store.js).
